day: Thursday of week 24 in Ordinary Time or Saint Robert Bellarmine, Bishop, Doctor or Saint Hildegard of Bingen, Virgin, Doctor
text:
There is something striking about the gap between knowing and loving. Paul recites the facts of faith with precision: Christ died, was buried, rose on the third day. These truths saved him and can save us. But notice what transforms a fact into a living gospel—it is love. The woman at the Pharisee's table knows nothing of theological formulas. What she knows is that she has been forgiven, and that knowledge has broken something open in her heart. Her tears, her hair, her kisses—these are not the language of doctrine but of overwhelming gratitude.

Paul himself understands this. He did not begin as a believer; he began as a persecutor. Something—someone—met him and changed him so completely that he could say, with strange humility, that he worked harder than anyone else, yet all the credit belonged to grace. He was reborn into a love he had not earned. Like the woman, his response was not merely to accept a truth but to spend his life in service to it.

Perhaps we sometimes keep our faith polite, orderly, safe. But both readings invite us into something wilder: the messy, grateful, unselfconscious love of one who knows they have been forgiven much. Not because the facts of faith are unimportant, but because facts only come alive when they touch our hearts and remake our lives.

What does it feel like, in this moment, to remember that you have been forgiven?
